policy_floor: Resource Ledger omission on a C++ diff (CLAUDE.md standing rule 2 policy floors; governance SKILL.md shared preamble)
trigger: the Gate 1 Resource Ledger is read as the complete ownership account of the diff
classification_rationale: the ledger listed the constructor's owners only, and two of its sentences were false for the diff as a whole: 'no second acquire' (the test takes a second lease) and 'no new ... temp path' (the test creates an ephemeral database)
summary: The Gate 1 Resource Ledger omitted the test hunk's owners. Fixed by amending the ledger (no C++ change for it). Amended text, re-reviewed by cpp-safety at Gate 8 (cs-1 closed): production code unchanged - the guard reuses the constructor's single pool lease (no second acquire in production code), `pg::PgResult probe` is RAII per loop iteration, `PQresultErrorMessage(probe.get())` is consumed inside the spdlog full-expression while `probe` is live, `kProjections` is static storage, `sql` is local per iteration; the loop has no `continue` (the probe is freed at iteration end and on the early return). Test code (rewritten in 3324566de): `db` = YUZU_REQUIRE_PG_DB_TPL, one non-copyable, non-movable PostgresTestDb clone per run, best-effort DROP DATABASE WITH (FORCE) in its destructor (logs 'leaked yuzu_test_*' if that fails); `pool` = PgPool (copy and move deleted), declared after `db`, its destructor waits for all leases; `intact`/`broken`/`restored` = SoftwareInventoryStore (copy deleted, so non-movable), each in its own block, holding no lease past construction; the catalog-read block has a move-only Lease and PgResult, names copied into std::string while the result is live; the `alter` lambda borrows `pool`, never escapes, its Lease and PgResult are released at lambda exit including on REQUIRE-throw unwind. No fd, HANDLE, socket, thread, subprocess, mapped library, filesystem temp path or manual cleanup (the ephemeral database is the test's one temporary resource). Gate 8 also confirmed CAPTURE copies its values, identifiers come from the test's own catalog and are double-quoted, and the production hunks are comment-only (comment-stripped SHA-256 identical).

waiver_rationale: The PR author (Doomgoose) directed on 2026-09-30 to leave this open for now because PR #5172 is one step of a longer roadmap that will cover it. This is an author-directed deferral, NOT an adjudication by a non-author; the ADR owner was not consulted and the finding is not closed. Tracker for the missing kind: #4432.
policy_floor: ADR-0008 (accepted), 2026-06-22 Update, normative requirement: the non-transactional migration kind must be built before a rewrite or index build on an already-large table ships
trigger: a release from main that carries migration v7 upgrades a deployment with a non-trivial installed_software table (schema v6 has shipped since v0.13.0); nothing in the record or in the release skill detects that 'no production fleet' has stopped being true
classification_rationale: the exception instrument the repo requires for shipping such a migration before the kind exists (a reviewed ADR-0008 exception, #4432 acceptance criteria) is absent; the ladder row records an accepted risk instead
summary: Reported independently by architect (ARCH-1), enterprise-readiness (EN-1) and compliance-officer (CO-1, contingent). v7 does a table rewrite and a plain CREATE INDEX in one transaction on installed_software, which is not born-empty. The same shape was ruled a policy-floor violation for app_perf_daily_store (#4432) and execution_tracker (#4624). OPEN by the PR author's direction: no non-author adjudication, the ADR owner was not consulted, the row is not closed. The repo text (ladder row, v7 comment, manual, fragment) records an accepted risk with accurate thresholds and cites #4432 only as the tracker of the missing kind; it does not claim compliance with ADR-0008 or a closure.

trigger: an operator or maintainer sizes a v7 upgrade from the ladder row, the manual or the release note: about 7k or more machines in a multi-replica deployment with an old-version replica still serving when the first v7 replica starts
classification_rationale: the recorded 'very large fleets / tens of minutes' wording was wrong (the hold passes the pool's 10 s lock_timeout from roughly 2-4M rows), the two timing sets disagreed (4 s + 6.5 s vs 8 s + 10 s), and the OfflineEndpointStore-v3 precedent clause did not hold for a table that grows with agents x kMaxEntries
summary: Reported by architect (ARCH-2), enterprise-readiness (EN-2/3/4), sre (sre-2), compliance-officer (CO-4), consistency-auditor (CA-1/3) and docs-writer (DW-L1/L2/L3, DW-C1); a second pass at Gate 8 (architect G8-A1..A4/A6..A8, docs-writer DW2-1..DW2-4) asked for further accuracy edits. Fixed in 3324566de and b3aa51cec: ladder row, v7 code comment, manual 'Upgrading' (rows-first, stop-every-replica above about 2M rows, free space and WAL, synchronous standby, DSN options, killed-backend behaviour, refusal diagnosis), changelog fragment. Not edited, per the approved plan: the PR body still quotes one timing run and the first governance pass (docs-writer DW2-5).

trigger: a reader relies on the is_open() doc, the guard comment or the test-coverage row for what closes the store or what is tested
classification_rationale: the docs are incomplete, not false: the constructor doc omitted the third close condition, the guard comment did not say it checks column presence only, and the coverage row omitted the new test
summary: Reported by happy-path, architect (ARCH-4), unhappy-path (UP-2/UP-4), docs-writer (DW-C2/D1/D2), consistency-auditor (CA-5), quality-engineer (QE-3) and compliance-officer (CO-4a). Fixed: .hpp constructor doc, guard comment ('column presence only', 'keep each list equal to its table's columns'), docs/test-coverage.md row.

trigger: a later edit deletes or truncates one of the three unpinned guard entries or one of 32 columns on a database whose schema_meta is current
classification_rationale: the test pinned 2 of the guard's 34 columns and used a fresh-migration fixture where the file's own header names the cloned template for DROP COLUMN tests
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-1/QE-2), consistency-auditor (CA-2), unhappy-path (UP-3/UP-5). Fixed in 3324566de: the test now runs on YUZU_REQUIRE_PG_DB_TPL and, for every (table, column) read from information_schema, renames the column away (store must be closed) and back (store must open). 214 assertions = 34 x 6 + 10. Mutation-checked on the committed test: guard neutered -> exactly the 34 columns fail; version_rollup entry removed -> exactly its 3; first_seen removed from one list -> exactly 1; a wrong column name in one list (false-positive direction) -> the control and the shared template builder fail. Gate 8 nits (QE2-1 CAPTURE(table) on the vacuity guard, QE2-2 rename to rename_prefix) folded into b3aa51cec.

trigger: the reply to the reviewer's ADR-0016 blocker is posted with the first-draft wording
classification_rationale: 'no reclassification' was falsifiable from ADR-0016 (operator-tier, 'never in this blob'), ADR-3007 is only proposed and covers install location only, and 'no REST, MCP or UI path' omitted direct SQL
summary: Reported by security-guardian (SG-2/SG-3), compliance-officer (CO-2), docs-writer (DW-A1..A5) and consistency-auditor (CA-4); re-checked at Gate 8 (DW2-6..DW2-9). Fixed in the posted reply: 'no reclassification' removed, ADR-3007 called proposed with its scope stated, the PR-body parenthetical attached to 'on purpose' only, 'the stored copies', direct SQL noted, the sequencing question reworded to 'before, or in the same change as', the ADR-0028 concession dropped, a tracker and the reconcile list added.

trigger: the agent-side PR is raised without the ADR-0016 amendment and the reconciliation of the docs that go false
classification_rationale: the earlier ledger row gov-agent-side-followups was recorded as deferred-to-issue #TBD and no issue existed while the reply promised the amendment 'before or with the agent-side PR'
summary: Reported by compliance-officer (CO-3), enterprise-readiness (EN-5), consistency-auditor (CA-6) and security-guardian (SG-2). Filed as #5186 (P1): agent-side mirror of the 16-field tail plus the ADR-0016 amendment and the doc reconciliation it forces.

trigger: restart while another session holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on a store table past lock_timeout, or a DSN with options= (no injected timeouts), or a dropped connection mid-probe
classification_rationale: the guard adds a refuse-to-boot cause with an under-specified log line (null result, no SQLSTATE, no schema_meta version), unbounded probes under a custom options DSN, and there is no ops-runbook entry
summary: Reported by security-guardian (SG-1), unhappy-path (UP-1/UP-4), sre (sre-1) and architect (focus 1). Accepted for this PR: ADR-0012 s1 makes construction fail closed and ApiTokenStore has the identical guard. Filed as #5187 (P2): guard log fallback and SQLSTATE across the three guard-bearing stores, boot deadlines under a custom options DSN, ops-runbook entry, playbook multi-table example, upgrading.md cross-references.

trigger: schema drift (or any store-open failure) on an unattended restart with no external up alert
classification_rationale: no shipped rule is a dead-man's-switch for the server process itself; true for every born-on-PG store and not made worse by the guard (before it, the same drift stayed green on /readyz and surfaced 5-15 minutes later through the inventory alerts)
summary: Pre-existing platform gap, tracked as #2956; the projection guard fails at the first boot after the drift instead.

trigger: an operator above the manual's 2M-row line upgrades on a volume without headroom or on a synchronous-standby profile, kills the server mid-migration and restarts at once, or follows the refusal example for a whole-database restore
classification_rationale: the manual stated the refusal cause as fact although the guard refuses on any probe error, gave an example that cannot produce the refusal (a whole-database restore rolls schema_meta back too), and said a kill 'discards the transaction' although the backend keeps the lock until Postgres notices the lost connection
summary: Gate 8 (architect G8-A1..A4, A6..A8; docs-writer DW2-1..DW2-4): fixed in b3aa51cec - refusal diagnosis ('usually', schema-only restore, transient errors are not a mismatch), disk/WAL/synchronous-standby note, killed-backend behaviour and pg_terminate_backend, systemd restart limit, single-node/one-host qualification, DSN options, 'stop every replica first if unsure', compose file named, fenced SQL, ladder/comment/fragment/.hpp wording. Not edited, per the approved plan: PR body (DW2-5).

trigger: a Compose operator upgrades a large installed_software table by the upgrading.md recipe (health check 'should be healthy', then a rollback recipe)
classification_rationale: the sibling upgrade path does not point at the schema v7 wait and its rollback block invites aborting the migration; a third document outside the approved scope of this cycle
summary: Gate 8 (architect G8-A5). Deferred: carried into #5187 as acceptance criterion 5 (cross-reference at the Docker recipe, checklist bullet, RPM postun note, the pre-existing /readyz mis-statement).

adjudicated_by: FortitudeEtc (PR reviewer, not the change's author), review 5394641495 on head 22df0c92f, which withdrew blocker 1 and recorded the maintainer's decision
adjudication_rationale: The blocker rested on ADR-0008 and the playbook requiring the non-transactional kind or a reviewed exception before a rewriting migration ships. The review states the maintainer decided that a hard cutover, not a rolling upgrade, is acceptable at this stage, that this is the exception those documents ask for, and that nothing in the code needs to change. The decision is recorded in the ladder row (docs/postgres-migration-ladder.md, SoftwareInventoryStore v7) in the same change that closes this row.
waiver_rationale: Hard cutover accepted for v7 at this stage (rolling upgrade not supported); stop every replica above about 2M rows, start one, let v7 finish. The online migration kind remains #4432.
summary: Closed by the reviewer's withdrawal of blocker 1 in review 5394641495 (non-author adjudication above); the rewrite is unchanged and documented as a hard cutover. This replaces the earlier author-directed deferral, which was not an adjudication by a non-author.
